terms.meaning: A ranked order where the gaps between steps are not known to be equal.
An object that cannot be changed after it is created.

used_by: packages/value/ (named in the docstring as where derived values are computed; its imports are not visible)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and the inverted-dimension list
sections.what: Explains what the module is for and sets up the list of dimensions where a higher score is worse. That list is the main protection against a rollup ranking the hardest processes as the best.
sections.why: The docstring says a rollup that gets the inversion wrong does so silently, so the list is exported for rollups to check against.
sections.watch_out: Any rollup that ranks by these scores must handle the two inverted dimensions in the opposite direction.

sections.name: ScoredDimension
sections.title: One scored judgement
sections.what: Defines one score: a whole number from 0 to 5, a one-line reason, and a list of evidence ids. An empty evidence list is allowed, but it marks the score as an unsupported hypothesis.
sections.why: The docstring says a bare number cannot be reviewed or calibrated, so a reason is required with every score.
sections.watch_out: The evidence list is required even when it is empty, so a missing field is rejected rather than treated as empty.

sections.name: Scorecard
sections.title: The nine-dimension scorecard
sections.what: Groups the nine scores for one process. Seven are higher-is-better. Fragmentation and change burden are inverted, so five means worse. The model is frozen after creation and rejects unknown fields.
sections.why: The docstring says the inverted scores are the most common source of scoring bugs, so the field descriptions repeat the warning.
sections.watch_out: Any code that averages, ranks or compares these nine scores must respect which two are inverted.

sections.name: NatureOfWork
sections.title: Four work-position values
sections.what: Four values from 0 to 100 that place the work on axes: manual to automated, physical to cerebral, judgement required, and coordination load. They describe where the work sits, not how good it is.
sections.why: The docstring says there is no good end of any axis, so ranking or averaging them is wrong and a recommendation should not come from one alone.
sections.watch_out: The rule against ranking or summing these values is written only in comments. Nothing in the code enforces it.

sections.name: OperatingModelImplication
sections.title: One operating-model consequence
sections.what: One effect on how the organisation is run if the future state is adopted. It is a written statement with a list of supporting evidence ids.
sections.why: The docstring says consequences are described qualitatively. Quantities are computed downstream.
sections.watch_out: The evidence list is required, so an empty list must be written on purpose to mark the consequence as unsupported.

sections.name: WorkforceImplication
sections.title: One workforce consequence
sections.what: Describes what happens to one role. It gives the role name, a direction of change from the headcount direction set, a list of skills the role gains, and evidence ids.
sections.why: The docstring says the model may give a direction only. Any magnitude must be computed from the cost basis, which only the value code knows.
sections.watch_out: The direction is the only workforce quantity allowed here. Adding a number field would let an unchecked total enter the record.

sections.name: Implications
sections.title: The full set of consequences
sections.what: Groups the operating-model consequences and the workforce consequences for the whole future state, with one evidence list for the block.
sections.why: The docstring says this block is qualitative only, so value figures, headcount, costs and timelines do not belong here.
sections.watch_out: The block-level evidence list is required, so a block with no items still needs the field to be present.

summary: Defines the judgements about a process: a nine-dimension scorecard, four work-position values, and the operating model and workforce consequences of a future state.
purpose: Records the qualitative assessment that the prioritisation grid is built from, in a form a computer can check.
why: The docstring states that scores are ordinal, positions are descriptive, and workforce impact is a direction only. Money and headcount totals are computed elsewhere so a model cannot invent them.
how: First defines the set of dimensions where a higher score is worse. Then defines the scored dimension (a whole number from 0 to 5, a reason, and an evidence list), the nine-dimension scorecard, the four work positions, the operating model item, the workforce item, and a container that groups the consequences. Every model is frozen after creation and rejects unknown fields.
inputs: Values produced by an upstream agent or a person, checked against these models when a record is built.
outputs: Validated scorecard and implication objects, or a validation error naming the field that broke a rule.
risks: A rollup that treats the two inverted dimensions as higher-is-better will rank the hardest processes as the best opportunities. Adding a numeric headcount field to the workforce item would let a model produce an unchecked total. Omitting an evidence list is an error, not a shortcut.
debug: If a record fails to load with a score error, check that each score is a whole number from 0 to 5 with a reason and an evidence list. If a dimension looks ranked the wrong way, check whether the rollup uses the inverted-dimension set.
